stem: Which of the following is a base physical quantity?
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: identify various physical quantities as base and derive quantities;

option_feedback.reason: Force (N = kg·m/s²) is a derived quantity expressed in terms of mass, length, and time.
Density (kg/m³) is a derived quantity obtained by dividing mass by volume.
Velocity (m/s) is a derived quantity obtained by dividing length (displacement) by time.

stem: The number 0.012345678 can be represented in scientific notation as
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: convert numerical values of measurement in scientific notation;

option_feedback.reason: Because 0.012345678 is less than 1, moving the decimal point 2 places to the right requires an exponent of -2, and only one non-zero digit precedes the decimal.
1.2345678 × 10² equals 123.45678, whereas moving the decimal 2 places to the right gives 10⁻².
Standard scientific notation requires a mantissa between 1 and 10 (1.2345678 × 10⁻², not 12.345678 × 10⁻²).

stem: All of the following quantities can be measured by using Vernier callipers EXCEPT
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: describe the working of measuring instruments;

option_feedback.reason: The narrow depth rod (strip) of Vernier callipers measures the depth of a beaker or hole.
The outer jaws of Vernier callipers measure the length of small objects.
The jaws of Vernier callipers measure internal and external diameter, whereas weight is a force measured by a spring balance.

stem: The number of significant figures in (25.01)^2 is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: describe significant figures;

option_feedback.reason: In multiplication, the result retains the same number of significant figures as the factor with the fewest significant figures (25.01 has 4 significant figures).
The trapped zero in 25.01 is significant, giving 4 significant figures rather than 3.
Although 25.01² = 625.5001 has 7 digits before rounding, significant figure rules limit the rounded result to 4 significant figures.

stem: In a classroom, a student got up from his/ her desk and walked 3 m ahead towards his/ her friend's desk. He/ she collected a book and walked 3 m back to his/ her own desk.\n\nThe total displacement of the student would be
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: define the following terms: a. distance, b. displacement, c. speed, d. velocity, e. acceleration;

option_feedback.reason: 3 m is the one-way distance to the teacher's table, whereas returning to the starting desk makes the net displacement 0 m.
6 m is the total distance travelled (3 m + 3 m), whereas displacement is the shortest directed distance between initial and final positions (0 m).
Since the student starts and ends at the exact same desk, initial and final positions coincide and displacement is 0 m.

stem: In the given speed-time graph, the sum of areas representing the total distance covered by a body is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: calculate the area under the speed-time graph of uniformly accelerated objects to find out the distance covered by the objects;

option_feedback.reason: Region Y lies outside the shaded speed-time curve and does not represent distance (area under the graph).
Region Y is above the graph line, whereas distance equals the area between the speed-time curve and the time axis (W + X + Z).
Only the regions underneath the speed-time line down to the horizontal time axis (W + X + Z) represent distance travelled.

stem: In the given distance-time graph, the line that represents a body in rest position is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: infer the following states of a body based on the given graph: a. at rest, b. moving with constant speed, c. moving with positive acceleration, d. moving with negative acceleration;

option_feedback.reason: Line A slopes upward from the origin, representing motion with constant positive speed.
Curve C has a changing slope, representing non-uniform (accelerated) motion.
Line D slopes downward toward the time axis, whereas horizontal line B has zero slope (distance does not change with time, so the body is at rest).

stem: All three equations of motion are applicable on bodies having uniform
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: calculate average speed, average velocity and acceleration;

option_feedback.reason: Uniform speed with zero acceleration needs only d = vt; the kinematic equations of motion apply more generally to any constant (uniform) acceleration.
If velocity is uniform, acceleration is zero; the three equations of motion govern motion under uniform acceleration.
Uniform momentum implies zero net force and zero acceleration, whereas the three equations of motion require uniform acceleration.

stem:
A cricket ball is hit in such a way that it travels vertically upward.

What will be its initial velocity, if it attains the maximum height in 3s?

(Note: Take the value of acceleration due to gravity as 9.8 m/s^2.)
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to free-falling bodies using the relation g = Δv/ Δt.

option_feedback.reason: 3.2 m/s does not use v_i = g × t = 9.8 m/s² × 3 s (taking 3 s to reach highest point where v_f = 0).
6.8 m/s subtracts 9.8 - 3.0 instead of multiplying g × t.
12.8 m/s adds 9.8 + 3.0 instead of using 0 = v_i - gt => v_i = 9.8 × 3 = 29.4 m/s.

stem: A force of 100 N acts on an object for 10 s. If the velocity of the object is 50 m/s, then the amount of momentum in the object will be
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to momentum and impulse;

option_feedback.reason: 10 Ns divides 100 N by 10 s instead of multiplying Impulse = Δp = F × t = 100 N × 10 s = 1000 Ns.
50 Ns confuses the given velocity (50 m/s) with change in momentum (F × t = 100 × 10 = 1000 Ns).
100 Ns is the force magnitude alone without multiplying by the 10 s time interval.

stem: If a body is taken to the surface of the moon, then which of the following physical quantities of the body will change?
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between mass and weight;

option_feedback.reason: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body and remains constant everywhere in the universe.
Length is a geometric dimension unaffected by gravitational field strength.
Density (ρ = m/V) depends on mass and volume, both of which remain unchanged on the Moon; only weight (W = mg) changes.

stem: In a tug of war, an inextensible rope is pulled by two teams in opposite direction over a central line. Each team has four players and each player is applying 10 N force on the rope.\n\nDuring the game, if the rope is balanced over the central line, then the tension in the rope will be
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: determine the resultant of two or more forces acting along the same straight line;

option_feedback.reason: Although the net horizontal force on the stationary rope is 0 N, the internal tension throughout the pulled rope is non-zero.
Each team of 4 members pulls with 4 × 10 N = 40 N, not 20 N.
In AKU-EB's official 2025 key, D (80 N) is the keyed response (summing the two 40 N pulls; note that ideal-string physics defines tension as 40 N).

stem: A passenger getting down from a moving bus falls forward. This is due to the
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: explain that the mass of an object resists changes from its state of rest or motion (inertia);

option_feedback.reason: A couple consists of two equal, opposite parallel forces separated by a distance, which does not cause a alighting passenger to pitch forward.
Friction stops the passenger's feet on the ground, while the upper body continues moving forward due to inertia of motion.
The primary physical property keeping the passenger's upper body moving forward at the bus's speed is inertia.

stem: If an object moves with the help of wheels from one point to another point on a rough surface, then the type of friction between wheels and surface is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between rolling friction and sliding friction;

option_feedback.reason: Static friction acts when surfaces are at rest relative to each other before motion starts.
Sliding friction occurs when an object is dragged without wheels.
Wheels convert sliding motion into rolling motion, so the opposing resistance is specifically rolling friction.

stem: All of the following are the examples of turning effect of force EXCEPT

options.A: Claw hammer removing a nail from wood
options.B: Forearm lifting a load about elbow joint

explanation: Spring balance operates on linear deformation (Hooke's law $F=kx$), not on turning moment/torque.

current_mapping.description: explain the turning effect of force by relating it to everyday life;

option_feedback.reason: A claw hammer pivots about its curved head to pull a nail using a turning moment (torque).
The human forearm rotates about the elbow joint (pivot) under the torque of the biceps muscle.
A spanner rotates a nut about its centre using torque, whereas a spring balance stretches linearly in a straight line without rotation.

stem: In the given figure, a uniform metre rod is balanced at its centre by a fulcrum. The distances $d_1$, $d_2$ and $d_3$ are equal to $10\text{ cm}$, $2\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$ respectively. If $F_1$ and $F_2$ are equal to $2\text{ N}$ and $5\text{ N}$ respectively, then the magnitude of $F_3$ will be
explanation: Applying principle of moments: Anti-clockwise torque = Clockwise torque. $(F_1 \times d_1) + (F_2 \times d_2) = F_3 \times d_3 \implies (2 \times 10) + (5 \times 2) = F_3 \times 5 \implies 20 + 10 = 5 F_3 \implies F_3 = 30 / 5 = 6\text{ N}$.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to the principle of moments;

option_feedback.reason: 2 N does not balance the clockwise moment; by the principle of moments, F₁d₁ = F₂d₂.
4 N produces an insufficient counter-moment to balance the metre rod.
10 N over-balances the rod; applying F₁d₁ = F₂d₂ gives the balanced weight of 6 N.

stem: Four different forces ($F_1, F_2, F_3$ and $F_4$) of the same magnitude are acting on the given metre scale. Which force produces the maximum torque?
explanation: Torque $\tau = F \times r$. Force $F_4$ acts at $0\text{ cm}$ while fulcrum is at $50\text{ cm}$, giving the longest moment arm $r = 50\text{ cm}$, producing maximum torque.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to the moment of force or torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of force;

option_feedback.reason: Force F₁ acts closer to the hinges (smaller moment arm), producing less torque than F₄.
Force F₂ acts at an acute angle or smaller perpendicular distance than F₄.
Force F₃ has a smaller moment arm than F₄, which acts perpendicularly at the farthest edge from the hinges.

stem: A point where the whole weight of a body acts vertically downward is called the
explanation: By definition, the centre of gravity is the point where the entire gravitational force/weight of an object is concentrated vertically downward.

current_mapping.description: define centre of gravity and centre of mass of a body;

option_feedback.reason: Centre of mass is the point where mass is symmetrically distributed (independent of gravity), whereas whole weight acts through the centre of gravity.
Point of contact is where two surfaces touch, not where the resultant weight acts.
Point of applied force is where an external push or pull is applied.

stem: Which of the following correctly describes the direction of the gravitational field at a point?

options.A: It is parallel to the object that creates the field.
options.B: It is perpendicular to the object that creates the field.
options.C: It always points away the object that creates the field.
options.D: It always points towards the object that creates the field.

explanation: Gravity is exclusively an attractive force, so gravitational field lines always point radially inward towards the mass creating the field.

current_mapping.description: define gravitational field strength;

option_feedback.reason: Gravitational field lines point radially inward toward the centre of the mass, not parallel to its surface.
Gravitational field is specifically directed radially *towards* the attracting mass (attractive only), not merely perpendicular in either direction.
Gravity is always an attractive force, so gravitational field lines never point away from the mass.

stem:
If the gravitational acceleration on the surface of the Earth is given, then the additional information required to determine the mass of the Earth using the law of gravitation would be

• I. radius of the Earth
• II. density of the Earth
• III. universal gravitational constant (G)
explanation: From $g = G M_e / R_e^2$, mass is $M_e = g R_e^2 / G$. Hence only radius ($R_e$) and gravitational constant ($G$) are required.

option_feedback.reason: Knowing g alone is not enough to find Earth's mass M = gR²/G; both Earth's radius R (I) and the gravitational constant G (III) are required.
The mass of the test object cancels out of g = GM/R² and provides no information about Earth's mass.
The object's mass (II) cancels out; you need the radius of the Earth (I) and universal gravitational constant G (III).

stem: If an astronaut attains a height equal to the radius of the Earth, then his weight related to the Earth surface will become
explanation: The distance from the center of the Earth becomes r = R_e + h = R_e + R_e = 2R_e. According to the law of gravitation, gravitational force varies inversely with the square of distance (F ∝ 1/r² = 1/(2R_e)² = 1/4 F₀). Therefore, his weight will become one-fourth of its value on the Earth's surface.

option_feedback.reason: At altitude h = R, the distance from Earth's centre doubles (r = 2R), and since g' = g(R/r)², weight becomes (1/2)² = 1/4th, not 1/2.
Moving farther from Earth's centre weakens gravity, so weight decreases rather than doubling.
By the inverse-square law W ∝ 1/r², doubling the distance from Earth's centre reduces weight to (1/2)² = one-fourth.

stem:
An artificial satellite is revolving around the Earth in a specific orbit. (F₁) is the magnitude of the force exerted by the Earth on a satellite and (F₂) is the magnitude of the force exerted by the satellite on the Earth.

Which of the following statements is TRUE for the given condition?
explanation: According to Newton's third law of motion and Newton's law of universal gravitation, mutual gravitational forces form an action-reaction pair. Since F₁ and F₂ represent the magnitudes of these mutual gravitational forces, their magnitudes are equal: F₁ = F₂.

current_mapping.description: explain Newton’s laws of motion;

option_feedback.reason: The question compares the *magnitudes* (F₁) and (F₂), which are both positive scalars and equal (F₁ = F₂) by Newton's third law.
By Newton's third law of motion, the Earth and the satellite exert equal gravitational forces on each other.
Despite the Earth's much larger mass, the gravitational pull of the Earth on the satellite equals the pull of the satellite on the Earth (F₁ = F₂).

stem: A traffic police car lifter lifts a car that was parked in a no parking area. The lifter lifts the car upto 0.5 m in the upward direction and the applied force is 5000 N. The work done on the car will be
explanation: Work done is given by W = F × d = 5000 N × 0.5 m = 2500 J.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to workdone;

option_feedback.reason: Only the vertical force (5000 N) does work over the vertical upward displacement of 0.5 m (W = 5000 × 0.5 = 2500 J); no work is done against gravity during horizontal motion at constant height.
10,000 J multiplies force by horizontal distance instead of vertical displacement in the direction of the lifting force.

stem:
During a football match, a strong wind shakes and loose a football of mass 0.40 kg that was stuck in a tree at a height of 20 m. Ignoring air resistance, the potential energy of the football when it was stuck in the tree was

(Note: Take the value of acceleration due to gravity as 9.8 m/s².)
explanation: Gravitational potential energy is given by P.E. = mgh = 0.40 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 20 m = 78.4 J.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to the kinetic and potential energy;

option_feedback.reason: 19.2 J does not match P.E = mgh = 0.40 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 20 m = 78.4 J.
31.4 J is an arithmetic error; multiplying 0.40 × 9.8 × 20 gives 78.4 J.
39.2 J is half the potential energy (forgetting a factor of 2 in 0.40 × 9.8 × 20 = 78.4 J).

stem: All of the following are the examples of renewable energy sources EXCEPT
explanation: Solar, wind, and geothermal energy are naturally replenished and considered renewable. Nuclear energy relies on finite deposits of radioactive elements like uranium and thorium, making it a non-renewable energy source.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between non-renewable and renewable energy sources with examples of each;

option_feedback.reason: Solar energy is continuously replenished by sunlight and is a renewable energy source.
Wind energy is naturally replenished by atmospheric heating and is renewable.
Geothermal energy from Earth's internal heat is renewable, whereas nuclear fission relies on finite uranium ore reserves (non-renewable).

stem: The kinetic energy of an object depends on
explanation: Kinetic energy $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ depends directly on mass and the square of velocity.

current_mapping.description: derive the formulae of kinetic energy K.E = ½ mv2 and potential energy P.E = mgΔh;

option_feedback.reason: Kinetic energy (K.E = ½mv²) depends on mass and velocity, not density.
Kinetic energy depends on instantaneous velocity (v), not rate of change of velocity (acceleration).
Macroscopic mechanical kinetic energy of a moving body is ½mv², determined by its mass and velocity.

stem:
If the mass of an elevator is $2000\text{ kg}$, then the work done to raise the elevator to a height of $50\text{ m}$ in $20\text{ seconds}$ will be
(Note: Take the value of acceleration due to gravity 'g' as $9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.)
explanation: Work done $W = mgh = 2000\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m/s}^2 \times 50\text{ m} = 980,000\text{ J}$. Time is redundant since work is asked, not power.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to workdone;

option_feedback.reason: 4 J divides 2000 by 500 instead of computing W = mgh = 2000 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 50 m = 980,000 J.
400 J omits multiplying by g and mass properly.

stem: A piece of wood is shown floating in four different liquids. Which liquid is denser than the others?
explanation: Liquid $X_4$ has the highest density because the wood floats highest above the surface with the least submerged volume, indicating greatest upthrust per unit submerged volume.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems using the relation of density;

option_feedback.reason: In liquid X₁, the wood block sinks deepest, meaning X₁ is the least dense liquid.
In X₂, more of the wood is submerged than in X₄.
By Archimedes' principle, the denser the liquid, the smaller the submerged volume needed to displace weight equal to the block—so X₄ (where the block floats highest) is the densest liquid.

stem:
Consider the given figure in which bricks of 1 kg are stacked in different positions.
Comparing stack X with the stack Y, the CORRECT statement is that

options.A: force of stack Y is greater than stack X.
options.B: force of stack X is greater than stack Y.
options.C: pressure of stack X is greater than stack Y.
options.D: pressure of stack Y is greater than stack X.

explanation: Both stacks have 3 bricks of 1 kg, so total weight/force is identical ($3\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ N/kg}$). However, Stack Y stands vertically with a smaller base area $A$, so pressure $P = F/A$ is greater for Stack Y.

current_mapping.description: explain that pressure varies with force and area with the help of real-life examples;

option_feedback.reason: Both stacks consist of the exact same number of identical 1 kg bricks, so their total downward weight (force) is equal.
Since both stacks have the same total mass, the downward force F = mg is identical for X and Y.
Stack Y stands on a smaller contact area on the ground than stack X, so for the same weight, Pressure P = F/A is greater for stack Y.

stem: As compared to sea level, the atmospheric pressure on mountains is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description:
describe that atmospheric pressure decreases with the increase 
in height above the earth’s surface;

option_feedback.reason: Atmospheric pressure decreases as altitude increases because the overlying air column becomes shorter and less dense.
Atmospheric pressure is highest at sea level and lower on high mountains.
Atmospheric pressure systematically decreases with elevation above sea level.

stem:
The height of Tarbela dam is 143 m.

Assuming that the dam is filled with water and the density of water is $1000\text{ kg/m}^3$. The value of acceleration due to gravity is $10\text{ m/s}^2$, the pressure exerted by water at the base of the dam will be
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to the relationship between pressure, depth and liquid density;

option_feedback.reason: 1.43 × 10⁷ Pa is 10× too large.

stem:
The weight of a ship is equal or less than the upthrust of the water acting on it.

The statement that will be TRUE for the ship is that it will

options.B: float on the surface of water.
options.C: initially float but then slowly sink into the water.
options.D: initially sink but then slowly come to the surface of water.

explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description:
discuss the use of Pascal’s law (including hydraulic press and 
hydraulic brakes on vehicles);

option_feedback.reason: An object sinks only when its downward weight exceeds the maximum upward upthrust of the displaced water.
As long as weight is less than or equal to upthrust, the net upward force keeps the ship floating in equilibrium.
By the principle of floatation, when weight ≤ upthrust, the ship floats continuously on the water surface.

stem: The body temperature of a patient is recorded as $101^{\circ}\text{F}$. This temperature is equal to
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

stem: The vessel that will cause a liquid to evaporate most quickly when containing equal amounts of the same liquid is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: describe factors that influence the rate of surface evaporation;

option_feedback.reason: Vessel A has a narrow opening/surface area, which restricts the rate of evaporation.
Vessel B has a smaller exposed liquid surface area than wide shallow dish D.
Vessel C has a smaller exposed surface area than vessel D; evaporation rate increases directly with surface area.

stem: All of the following show transfer of heat by convection EXCEPT the use of

options.B: hot air to fly off air balloons.
options.C: gas heaters to heat up rooms.

explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description:
explain convection in liquids and gases in terms of density changes with reference to the following real-life examples:
a. gliders,
b. flying of birds,
c. land breezes and sea breezes;

option_feedback.reason: Fans circulate air currents over skin, involving forced convection.
Hot air balloons rise because heated air expands, becomes less dense, and rises by convection.
Gas room heaters warm air that circulates throughout the room via convection currents, whereas a heating pad in direct contact with muscles transfers heat by conduction.

stem:
The vacuum in the thermos bottle prevents heat transfer by

• I. radiation
• II. conduction
• III. convection
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description:
discuss everyday applications of conduction, convection and radiation including:
a. heating objects such as kitchen pans,
b. heating of room by convection,
c. measuring temperature using an infrared thermometer,
d. using thermal insulation to maintain the temperature of a liquid and to reduce thermal energy transfer in buildings,
e. the mechanism of a household hot-water system;

option_feedback.reason: Infrared radiation (I) is an electromagnetic wave that travels easily across a vacuum (it is stopped by the silvered walls, not the vacuum).
The vacuum eliminates both conduction (II) and convection (III) because both require a material medium of molecules.
Radiation (I) can cross a vacuum, whereas conduction (II) and convection (III) are prevented by the absence of air molecules in the vacuum.

stem: The characteristic that should be present in a surface to protect it from infrared radiation is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: describe the effect of surface colour (black or white) and texture (dull or shiny) on the emission, absorption and reflection of infrared radiation;

option_feedback.reason: A good absorber would rapidly absorb incoming infrared heat rather than protecting the wearer.
A good absorber heats up rapidly when exposed to infrared radiation.
Note: Official 2025 key marks C (while physically Kirchhoff's law states shiny protective surfaces are both poor absorbers and poor emitters, D).

stem: The surface that is the good radiator of heat is
explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

current_mapping.description: describe the effect of surface colour (black or white) and texture (dull or shiny) on the emission, absorption and reflection of infrared radiation;

option_feedback.reason: Note: Official 2025 key marks B (white), whereas physically a dull black surface (A) is the best emitter/radiator of thermal radiation.
Green surfaces have intermediate emissivity.
Polished silver is a very poor radiator (emitter) and a strong reflector of heat.
